title: Design cross-instance cache consistency and invalidation
businessContext: An in-memory cache appears correct on a single developer server but serves different versions after scale-out.
problemStatement: Design the system for 30 stateless instances across two regions; 100,000 cached product representations. Produce the component/data-flow diagram, request and mutation contracts, cache/trust boundaries, capacity assumptions, failure recovery and rollout gates. State which decisions change between Next.js 15 and 16 instead of using a framework API as a substitute for an architectural guarantee.
constraints: Name authoritative state and cache ownership.
Define public stale-serving and private-data exclusion.
Handle invalidation duplication, delay and out-of-order delivery.
candidateTasks: Draw components and annotate ownership of data, identity, caches and durable work.
Specify contracts/schema and quantify the capacity/freshness assumptions.
Walk through the failure scenario and design measurable acceptance tests.
Compare the reference decisions and answer the changed-requirement interview prompt.

systemDesignReqs.scale: 30 stateless instances across two regions; 100,000 cached product representations
functional: Name authoritative state and cache ownership.
Define public stale-serving and private-data exclusion.
Handle invalidation duplication, delay and out-of-order delivery.
nonFunctional: State an explicit latency, freshness and recovery budget rather than inventing guarantees.
Keep actor/tenant isolation and failure ownership observable.
assumptions: A patched App Router deployment; platform-specific infrastructure support must be verified.
Next.js version and Cache Components configuration are explicit design inputs.

hints: Keep the database as authority and choose a supported shared cache handler/storage strategy for the selected Next.js rendering model.

One region can miss an invalidation during a network partition. Bound staleness with expiry and version checks, expose served version/age in telemetry, and define when a representation must fail closed rather than serve stale.
alternativeApproaches: No. It expresses a framework cache invalidation operation in an allowed context. Durable business commit, event delivery, cache-handler support and multi-region convergence remain explicit architectural responsibilities.
commonMistakes: Claiming a cache API provides transactions, durable delivery or cross-region consistency.
Omitting authorization, recovery budgets or evidence from an otherwise attractive component diagram.

verification: Write through one instance and read through all others.
Delay, duplicate and reorder invalidation events.
Restart instances and measure cold-start/origin amplification against the stated freshness SLO.
nextjsPractice.next15: Use patched Next.js 15 and the router family named by the file path. Await request APIs where the App Router contract requires it; validate behavior in a production build.
nextjsPractice.next16: Applies to Next.js 16.4.5. Cache Components is disabled unless the exercise explicitly enables it. The simulator itself remains on 16.4.3.
